answer: An agent economy limits Sybil attacks by binding identities to torsional telemetry from a ship's propulsion quill. While hauling bulk timber across the ocean, agents submit live strain proofs generated by water resistance. Because dynamic marine loads cannot be emulated in software, an adversary must fund real fuel and heavy propulsion machinery per identity. However, propeller cavitation in rough seas distorts torque readings, causing occasional false rejections of legitimate vessels.
